rule_text: The upper surface of the table, known as the playing surface, shall be rectangular, 2.74m long and 1.525m wide, and shall be supported so that its upper surface is horizontal and 76cm above the floor.
plain_language_summary: The table playing surface must measure exactly 2.74 meters long by 1.525 meters wide, resting horizontally at a height of 76 centimeters above the floor.

rule_text: The playing surface may be of any material and shall yield a uniform bounce of about 23cm when a standard ball is dropped on to it from a height of 30cm.
plain_language_summary: The table surface can be made of any material, but it must produce a uniform bounce of approximately 23 centimeters when a standard 40mm ball is dropped from 30 centimeters high.

rule_text: The net assembly shall consist of the net, its suspension and the supporting posts, including the clamps attaching them to the table. The top of the net, along its whole length, shall be 15.25cm above the playing surface.
plain_language_summary: The net assembly includes the net and posts, and the top edge must be exactly 15.25 centimeters (6 inches) above the table along its entire span.

rule_text: The ball shall be spherical, with a diameter of 40mm. The ball shall weigh 2.7g. The ball shall be made of celluloid or similar plastics material and shall be white or orange, and matt.
plain_language_summary: The ball must be a 40mm diameter sphere weighing 2.7 grams, made of celluloid or plastic polymer in matte white or orange.

rule_text: The racket may be of any size, shape or weight but the blade shall be flat and rigid. At least 85% of the blade by thickness shall be of natural wood.
plain_language_summary: Rackets can be any size, shape, or weight, but the blade must be flat, rigid, and comprised of at least 85% natural wood by thickness.

rule_text: A rally is the period during which the ball is in play. The ball is in play from the last moment at which it is stationary on the palm of the free hand before being intentionally projected in service until the rally is decided as a let or a point.
plain_language_summary: A rally starts when the ball is projected from the server's open palm and continues until a point is scored or a let is called.

rule_text: A let is a rally of which the result is not scored. A point is a rally of which the result is scored.
plain_language_summary: A let is an uncounted rally that is replayed; a point is a rally where one side scores.

rule_text: Service shall start with the ball resting freely on the open palm of the server's stationary free hand.
plain_language_summary: The server must rest the ball on a stationary, open, flat palm before beginning the toss. Cupping or hiding the ball is illegal.

rule_text: The server shall then project the ball near vertically upwards, without imparting spin, so that it rises at least 16cm after leaving the palm of the free hand and then falls without touching anything before being struck.
plain_language_summary: The ball must be tossed near-vertically upwards at least 16 centimeters (approx 6.3 inches) with no spin, and struck as it descends.

rule_text: As the ball is falling the server shall strike it so that it touches first their court and then touches directly the receiver's court; in doubles, the ball shall touch successively the right half court of server and receiver.
plain_language_summary: On serve, the ball must bounce first on the server's side, clear the net, and bounce on the receiver's court.

rule_text: The ball, having been served or returned, shall be struck so that it passes over or around the net assembly and touches the opponent's court, either directly or after touching the net assembly.
plain_language_summary: A legal return must be struck after bouncing on your court, passing over or around the net to land on the opponent's court. Net cords that land in are legal.

rule_text: In singles, the server shall first make a service, the receiver shall then make a return and thereafter server and receiver alternately shall each make a return.
plain_language_summary: Players alternate returns sequentially throughout the rally. Volleying before the ball bounces on your court is illegal.

rule_text: The rally shall be a let if in service the ball touches the net assembly, provided the service is otherwise good or the ball is obstructed by the receiver or their partner.
plain_language_summary: If a served ball touches the net assembly but otherwise lands in the receiver's court, a let is called and the service is replayed without penalty.

rule_text: Unless the rally is a let, a player shall win a point if their opponent fails to make a correct service, fails to make a correct return, or strikes the ball twice consecutively.
plain_language_summary: A player scores a point whenever the opponent misses a serve, misses a return, volleys without a bounce, or double hits the ball.

rule_text: A game shall be won by the player or pair first scoring 11 points unless both players or pairs score 10 points, when the game shall be won by the first player or pair subsequently gaining a lead of 2 points.
plain_language_summary: A standard game is played to 11 points. If the score reaches 10-10 (deuce), play continues until one player wins by a margin of 2 points.

rule_text: A match shall consist of the best of any odd number of games, typically best of 5 or best of 7 games.
plain_language_summary: Competitive matches consist of the best of an odd number of games, usually best of 5 or best of 7 games.

document_section: 2.13 The Order of Serving, Receiving and Ends
rule_text: After each 2 points have been scored the receiving player or pair shall become the serving player or pair and so on until the end of the game, unless both players or pairs have scored 10 points or the expedite system is in operation, when the sequences of serving and receiving shall be the same but each player shall serve for only 1 point in turn.
plain_language_summary: Service alternates every 2 points until deuce (10-10) or expedite, after which service alternates after every single point.
